title: Ask HN: Should we shut down current AI strategy? Vent Your Heart Out
summary:
I don't know, maybe it's just me.

Does it feel to you like we're boiling the oceans in a desperate attempt to build something "smarter than human?"

Do you notice that the idea that "AI will cure cancer" is predicated on the belief that we've found the data that will lead to a cure and us humans just somehow missed it?

Are you also watching your former boss, who laid you off for AI, slowly turn the nail gun that is AI automation towards his own face?

Are you also currently avoiding plane flights at all costs?

Personally, I like AI a lot, but I think conversational language models were a mistake. Isn't this the root of AI psychosis for most? Isn't autocomplete turned conversational just sycophancy for our delusions even if we have guardrails in place?

Don't you think that if you can't explain the functionality of an AI model that means you probably shouldn't use it?

If you said yes to any of the above I'd love to hear your thoughts on the current state of things. Please, vent your heart out.

If you said no to everything please just be quiet, this will be fun for the rest of us.

title: Ask HN: Can world models lead to racisim? Are there any Alignment frameworks?
summary:
I have never felt or believed in Dooms day theories about AI. But below is one of only 2 occasions where I am feeling AI can be too dangerous.

While building world model for enterprise decisions, I am intrigued by how far the AI can go out of reach.

Got to know - that now world models can learn from emotions & genetics.

That means - actually predicting the outcome & behavior of humans. If going unabated - so the builder can bring in bias. It sounds Deja vu for when the racist theories developed in wraps of the scholarly research in 1900s.

When I understand how the world model is gonna work - practically emotions & genetics aren't very far away from being built. There are already startups working on it.

While ours is only for Enterprise decisions, the one on genetics as world-wide population scale impact.

For World Models for Physical AI or Humanoids - this is more of physical tasks. I don't call it dangerous as there are quite a few checks & controls.

But when world models are used for Genetics - this has far reaching unabated repercussions on how humans bheave with each other. As models become more powerful, ppl will start relying on it.

I am not sure how the alignment of World Models will happen? LLMs are tbh primitive in nature.

For World Models alignment - are there any specific efforts or initiatives wroking on it?

We would be glad to include any alignment frameworks in our Benchmarking for Enterprise decisions. To monitor & remove bias.

title: How are large companies not ripshit about the frontier labs?
summary:
I am utterly baffled that the entire world is not coming after Anthropic and OpenAI with pitchforks. We are essentially funding:

1.The largest intellectual property theft from humanity in history, including corporate IP

2. Outrageous amount of money being spent with no real upside to show at this point. Can anyone name one positive thing that's come from AI so far objectively?

3. Non stop threats and attacks and greater and greater risk of bad actors engaging in cyber attacks.

4. Untold disruption to the economy and jobs

5. Untold risk from bioweapons

6. Increased instability in multiple sectors

7. Unknown risks to human intellect, development, and emotional well being

I could go on.

I just don't understand how large companies and governments all over the world aren't beside themselves with anger and rage. I could understand if we were seeing tangible improvements to work, society, and the products we use on a daily basis, but as someone who works for a very very large company who is embracing AI, we have seen almost 0 net benefit, with most people feeling burnt out, unhappy, scared, and overworked.

summary:
Some fish exhibit negligible senescence and routinely live for over 100 years. It seems our team has identified the gene directly responsible for this phenomenon. Even more excitingly, this gene is switched off in many people who don't make it past 80.

We've switched this gene on in mice and observed a 9% increase in median lifespan.

We're not going to reveal the gene's name until we develop a working antibody that can reliably switch it off in humans. But if you're curious, you could join our team as an early angel investor.

Let's talk. This might be your chance to live longer—and much better. You know what I mean.

title: Ask HN: Anyone else blurting?
summary:
Like most, I was stoked on LLMs when they became available. Particularly on the earlier free tiers where the slightly questionable answers were offset by generous tokens.

Now, I'm finding that having to use this tech is becoming much less fun. The constant corrections, the constant prompting for greater brevity, the grating certainty and sycophancy.

Others probably are forgiving considering the net benefit. But for me it honestly now feels like a chore, which is reflected in how my frustration is now appearing in how I communicate to it now.

Instead of articulating and making my prompts precise, I'm just straight-out blurting. Typos, missed words, poor semantic structure - I guess I maybe at some point reasoned that "it will get the picture, so why waste effort being articulate?" Or maybe I'm just anticipating that it is going to get it 15 percent wrong, so why even try and be articulate. Just blurt and steer. Blurt and steer.

Is anyone else finding this? I actually sometimes worry about it. I feel it's not just the fact that I'm offloading my cognition to it that is making me dumber, it is the way I'm communicating with it. They say the act of writing is tied to the act of thinking, and my prompts are basicslly the typographic equivalent of grunting right now.

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50537272
